handback.title: Setup gathers and stores a subscription's inputs
handback.summary: A setup command takes a subscription's inputs once and puts each where runs find it.
handback.user_story: The owner gives a subscription's inputs once; setup stores the key or sign-in and writes the settings file.

acceptance_criteria.text: Setup lists the inputs a subscription needs: membership, region, sign-in or key, and model.
acceptance_criteria.words: grabbing the inputs a user needs for a subscription (membership, region, sign-in or key, model)
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: It takes no input, so there is nothing missing or malformed to handle.

acceptance_criteria.text: Setup stores a key the owner gives as a repo secret, under the name the owner chooses.
acceptance_criteria.words: sign-in or key, model) and putting them in place

edge_cases.case: An empty key is refused and nothing is stored.
GitHub refuses the secret: setup fails and names it.

acceptance_criteria.text: The settings file lists the subscription with its agent and its secret's name, never the key itself.

edge_cases.case: Adding a second subscription keeps the first one and its roles.

acceptance_criteria.text: Setup signs the agent in through its own login, with the region the owner gives.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: A failed login is covered where the sign-in is stored: nothing is stored.

acceptance_criteria.text: Setup stores the files the agent's login saved as a repo secret.
acceptance_criteria.words: region, sign-in or key, model) and putting them in place

edge_cases.case: The login fails: setup fails and stores nothing.

acceptance_criteria.text: The settings file gives each role the owner names the subscription and model the owner gives.
acceptance_criteria.words: `roles` (planner, worker, reviewer: which subscription and model)
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Keeping earlier roles is covered under the subscription criterion; the inputs are plain names.
